ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against the OFAC SDN List, United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, Canadian Special Economic Measures Act sanctions lists, and the Canadian Consolidated Sanctions List (Global Affairs Canada); PEP status must be determined for all UBOs, directors, and signatories using a risk-based enhanced due diligence standard, with formal escalation for domestic or foreign PEPs, and ongoing adverse-media and politically exposed persons monitoring during the corporate lifecycle.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: BC Corporate Online (one-stop business registry), operated by BC Registry Services under the Ministry of Finance: https://www.corporateonline.gov.bc.ca
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: English is the primary required language; names must be fully expressed in Roman characters; alternate French-language legal elements are permitted but the principal distinguishing element must be in English. For federal and cross-border branding, a NUANS-style or BC Business Name Approval report is mandatory; any foreign-language transliteration must be certified and approved for identification purposes.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a rejection of a name approval request under section 22 of the BC Business Corporations Act, the applicant may file a written request for administrative review with the Director of Corporate Registries within 30 days of the rejection notice; the appeal must set out the grounds for distinctiveness and non-confusion with existing or reserved names. If the Director upholds the refusal, a further judicial review may be sought in the Supreme Court of British Columbia. No extension of the 56-day reservation is available; after expiry the applicant must re-file the name request.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: No virtual office recognised for the registered office requirement. The BC Business Corporations Act requires a registered office that is a physical location in British Columbia and the office address must be a genuine street address of a commercial premises capable of receiving service of process. A PO box or virtual mail scanning facility is not acceptable for the registered office. Virtual offices may only be used for secondary administrative functions such as bookkeeping or brand management, never for corporate registry service.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: 15–25% probability of a physical document/registered-office verification visit by BC Registry compliance officers or successors within a 12-month operating cycle; municipal food safety and public health inspections of the underlying ghost-kitchen premises are virtually certain (90–100%) because of the food-service licence engagement, and such visits may check corporate signage and consistency of commercial substance.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act, SBC 2002, c. 57, ss. 190-191 (incorporation application and certificate), s. 32 (notice of articles), s. 229 (registered office), s. 128 (director residency); Business Corporations Regulation, BC Reg. 51/2004.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, BC Registry Services, Ministry of Finance, Province of British Columbia (electronic filing via Corporate Online portal).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 1 - Application for Incorporation, accompanied by Form 2 - Notice of Articles and the company's Articles.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under the BC Business Corporations Act; incorporation with no-par-value common shares is permitted, and shares may be issued for such consideration as the directors accept (commonly a nominal CAD 0.0001 per share). No escrow account or paid-up capital deposit is required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: WHEREAS the Company was incorporated under the Business Corporations Act (British Columbia) on [date]; NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED that the subscription for 100 common shares without par value by the founding shareholders is accepted, allotted, and deemed fully paid. FURTHER RESOLVED that the registered office of the Company is fixed at 1234 Industrial Way, Richmond, British Columbia, Canada. FURTHER RESOLVED that the following officers be and are hereby appointed: [Name], President and Chief Executive Officer; [Name], Chief Financial Officer; and [Name], Corporate Secretary. FURTHER RESOLVED that the fiscal year end is December 31 and the board is authorized to open bank accounts, obtain municipal business licences, secure food premises permits, and execute all ancillary filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a pre-filing name search on Corporate Online or obtain a NUANS report to verify availability. Submit an electronic Name Reservation Request to secure an approved name for 56 days. The proposed name must include a legal element such as Inc., Corp., or Ltd., and must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing BC or federal corporate name.
required_dossiers: Consent to use of personal name or existing business name, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, select and submit up to three alternate names; no incorporation filing fee is lost because the CAD 350 charge is levied only at the Form 1 application stage.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Incorporation Application and Issuance of Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, BC Registry Services - Corporate Online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and file Form 1 - Application for Incorporation together with Form 2 - Notice of Articles and the company's Articles. The Notice of Articles must state the authorized share structure (e.g., unlimited common shares without par value), at least one director who is ordinarily resident in Canada, the registered office address, and the records office address. Pay the CAD 350 filing fee and submit electronically.
required_dossiers: Consent of each director to act (s. 124 BCBCA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Corporate Online validates the record; if the Notice of Articles is rejected, correct the identified fields and resubmit the same draft or initiate a new incorporation filing. The Certificate of Incorporation is issued retroactively only upon a complete and compliant submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organization of Statutory Corporate Records and Minute Book
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered office of the Company / external legal counsel (records retention per ss. 226-231 BCBCA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Assemble the statutory records book: Certificate of Incorporation, Notice of Articles, Articles, register of directors, register of shareholders, register of officers, share certificates, director consents, and minutes of the First Board Resolution. The records book must be kept at the registered office and made available to directors and shareholders.
required_dossiers: Register of directors, officers, and shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate of Incorporation contains an error, apply to the Registrar for a Certificate of Correction under s. 238 BCBCA; for internal minute book errors, pass a corrective board resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: CRA Business Number and GST/HST Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency - Business Registration Online (Canada.ca)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register for a 9-digit Business Number (BN) using the Certificate of Incorporation. Enrol for GST/HST (voluntary registration if annual gross revenue is below CAD 30,000), payroll deductions (CPP/EI) if employees are hired, and the corporate income tax account. A BC company must file an annual T2 corporate income tax return.
required_dossiers: Business activity description (NAICS 722513 - ghost kitchen / delivery-only food service)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If online registration is queried, verify director identification and registered office data; alternatively, submit paper Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number) to the CRA tax centre with an effective date aligned to the incorporation date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register for a BC Provincial Sales Tax (PST) account on eTaxBC. Prepared food sold through delivery platforms is generally subject to PST at 7% and GST at 5%. PST registration is compulsory when taxable sales in BC exceed CAD 10,000 in a calendar quarter; earlier voluntary registration is recommended.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registration is denied or placed under review, reconcile the projected revenue figures and resubmit; escalate unresolved matters to the Ministry of Finance registration desk because directors may be personally liable for uncollected PST.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business Licence and Zoning Approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal business licence office of the applicable city (e.g., City of Richmond or City of Vancouver)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a general business licence describing the delivery-only multi-brand ghost kitchen operation. Confirm that the leased industrial or commercial unit is zoned for food preparation and delivery-only sales. Attach the lease, corporate documents, and fire and health pre-clearance letters. Pay the annual licence fee and post the licence onsite.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement or title to premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the licence is refused on zoning grounds, file a discretionary development permit application or temporary use permit with the municipal planning department; remediation of operational concerns followed by resubmission resolves most non-zoning refusals.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local health authority environmental health division (Vancouver Coastal Health, Fraser Health, or Interior Health as applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a Food Premises Application under the Food Premises Regulation (BC Reg. 210/99) prior to opening. Include a HACCP plan covering each virtual brand's menu, hot and cold holding charts, and delivery temperature monitoring. The pre-opening inspection verifies the three-compartment sink, hand-washing stations, grease interceptor, pest control, and ventilation before the permit is issued.
required_dossiers: HACCP plan and menu matrix per virtual brand
Detailed floor plan of the kitchen
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the inspection identifies deficiencies, implement the inspector's corrective action plan and request re-inspection, which is typically scheduled within 5 working days; no food sales may occur until the operating permit is issued.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: WorkSafeBC Occupational Clearance and Fire Safety Certification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: WorkSafeBC - Industry & Labour Services; municipal fire department / Office of the Fire Commissioner
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company as an employer with WorkSafeBC. Install a UL 300-rated commercial cooking hood suppression system, fire extinguishers, emergency lighting, and exit signage. Obtain a professional engineer's certification of structural floor loads for deck ovens, combi ovens, and walk-in refrigeration. Secure the fire clearance and occupancy certificate before commissioning gas and electrical services.
required_dossiers: UL 300 hood suppression system servicing certificate
Fire safety plan approved by the fire prevention branch
Occupancy or possession certificate for the industrial unit
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If final fire clearance is withheld, apply for a temporary occupancy certificate subject to a written remediation schedule; complete the listed corrective actions and obtain final clearance, or appeal the inspection findings in writing to the municipal fire commissioner's office.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: BC Ministry of Health and regional health authorities (Vancouver Coastal Health / Fraser Health), together with the municipal business licence office; environmental oversight by the BC Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy and Metro Vancouver.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Food Service Establishment Operating Permit (Delivery-Only Multi-Brand Cloud Kitchen) issued under the Public Health Act and Food Premises Regulation, BC Reg. 210/99.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: BC Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy - Environmental Assessment Office (EAO); with municipal/regional permitting by Metro Vancouver.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration - small-scale delivery-only food production premise; not a reviewable project under the Environmental Assessment Act, SBC 2018, c. 51, but requires registration with the local health authority and compliance with Metro Vancouver sewer and air quality bylaws.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: grease interceptor sized per Metro Vancouver Sewer Use Bylaw No. 299 with an oil-and-grease limit not exceeding 50 mg/L and a monthly maintenance log; no process liquids to storm drains. Air emissions: commercial kitchen exhaust hoods must meet Metro Vancouver ambient air quality objectives for odour and VOCs, with ventilation in accordance with ASHRAE 154. Solid waste: used cooking oil and grease trap contents must be removed by a licensed recycler and stored onsite in sealed, labelled containers.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification per the BC Fire Code for commercial cooking operations, including annual servicing of the UL 300 hood suppression system; structural load inspection of the leased unit to confirm floor capacity for commercial kitchen equipment; WorkSafeBC occupational health and safety clearance; FOODSAFE Level 2 supervision; and municipal occupancy permit issued before operations commence.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC) - Business Registration Online (BRO), My Business Account (MyBA), and GST/HST NETFILE (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html); provincial counterpart for British Columbia sales tax: BC Ministry of Finance, Consumer Taxation Branch, via the eTaxBC portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entity procedure: (1) establish Canadian legal presence - incorporate under the BC Business Corporations Act via BC Corporate Online, or federally under the Canada Business Corporations Act via Corporations Canada followed by BC extra-provincial registration; (2) obtain the 9-digit CRA Business Number (BN), the statutory tax ID, through Business Registration Online, which simultaneously opens the GST/HST (RT), payroll (RP), and corporate income tax (RC) program accounts; non-residents without Canadian registration must file CRA Form RC3486, evidence commercial activity in Canada, and may be required to post security under ETA s.296 and maintain accessible books and records under ETA s.291.1; (3) register separately for BC Provincial Sales Tax (PST) with the BC Ministry of Finance through eTaxBC; and (4) obtain municipal business and food-premises licences (City of Vancouver business licence and regional health authority food permit) as practical operating preconditions.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no US-style check-the-box election; entity classification follows CBCA/BCBCA corporate law, and corporations are fully taxed at entity level under ITA Part I. Available statutory elections include: the GST/HST closely-related corporation election (ETA s.156) treating intercompany taxable supplies as made for nil consideration; ITA s.256 associated-corporation elections to allocate the small business deduction; ITA s.83(2) capital dividend account election; corporate fiscal-period and partnership elections; and hybrid-mismatch rate-differential elections with EIFE (excessive interest and financing expenses) designated-group elections under ITA s.18.4-18.9 for cross-border financing structures.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (federal Goods and Services Tax at 5%) plus British Columbia Provincial Sales Tax (PST at 7% on prepared food) - combined 12% effective indirect rate on delivery meals; British Columbia is a non-HST province since the April 2013 HST repeal, so the 15% HST does not apply.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: GST/HST small-supplier threshold: C$30,000 of worldwide taxable supplies (including zero-rated supplies, excluding sales of capital property and financial services) over the trailing four calendar quarters under ETA s.240; mandatory registration is triggered once exceeded, and meal sales through UberEats and DoorDash count as taxable supplies. BC PST: a vendor with a place of business in BC must register immediately; an extraprovincial (out-of-province) vendor must register once BC taxable sales exceed C$10,000 in a 12-month period.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not operate a real-time fiscal clearance, e-invoice stamping, or digital control-authority regime. Registrants must issue a valid GST/HST tax invoice under ETA s.221 containing the BN, transaction date, identification of the parties, taxable status of each supply, consideration, and the GST/HST amount or a tax-inclusive statement; electronic invoices are accepted. Mandatory electronic filing applies through GST/HST NETFILE and eTaxBC, and registrants with annual taxable revenues above C$1.5M must file electronically. Payment service providers, including UberEats and DoorDash payouts, are subject to the CRA Electronic Payment Transaction Reporting Regime (REEPT) for payments processed from 2024, giving CRA transaction-level visibility into ghost-kitchen revenue.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available under ETA Schedule VI, Part V: (i) tangible personal property (including packaged or prepared meals sold for export) is zero-rated if the supplier ships or delivers the goods outside Canada, normally within 60 days of the supply (s.1-5); (ii) services supplied to a non-resident person are zero-rated under s.7 where the service is not acquired for consumption in Canada and the non-resident is not a GST/HST registrant; and (iii) domestic meal supplies through Canadian delivery platforms remain taxable at 5% GST plus 7% BC PST, and no basic-grocery zero-rating applies to prepared food.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Canada GCA/CAARS automated export reporting or equivalent commercial export documentation)
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / carrier certificate proving physical export from Canada within the prescribed 60-day window
Inward Remittance Certificate (or bank payment records) evidencing FX settlement from the non-resident buyer
Commercial invoice and export sales contract identifying the foreign purchaser and HS classification of the meal products
Packing list and container manifest linking the specific consignment to the zero-rated sale
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA has full reassessment and input tax credit clawback powers over fraudulent or unsupported export zero-rating: gross-negligence penalty of the greater of C$325 and 50% of the tax sought to be evaded (ETA s.285); false-declaration and evasion penalties with daily penalties (ETA s.280.1 and s.281); retrospective reassessment of uncollected GST/HST plus arrears interest (ETA s.280); criminal prosecution under ETA s.283 and ITA s.239 with fines up to 200% of the evaded amount and imprisonment of up to 5 years; and, for cross-border arrangements, a transfer-pricing penalty of 10% of the net adjustment. Substantiation of physical export and FX repatriation within the 180-day ceiling is critical, as CRA audit staff use carrier export filings, customs data, and REEPT payment-platform reports to cross-match zero-rated export claims.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) as the monetary and financial stability authority; foreign exchange administration and exchange control policy are vested in the Minister of Finance under the Currency Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-52, with operational oversight shared by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI), the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) for cross-border electronic fund transfer surveillance under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA), the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) for trade declaration data under the Customs Act, and Statistics Canada for Balance of Payments statistical reporting.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar (CAD) is fully convertible on both current-account and capital-account transactions. Canada has been an IMF Article VIII member and does not impose exchange controls, prior approval requirements, or restrictions on the conversion, transfer, remittance, or repatriation of funds for a British Columbia business corporation. Dividends, royalties, repatriated capital, intercompany loan repayments, and settlement proceeds may be converted and remitted freely in any currency. The principal compliance frictions are (i) Part XIII of the Income Tax Act non-resident withholding tax of 25% on certain cross-border payments, reduced by applicable tax treaties; (ii) FINTRAC large-value EFT reporting at or above C$10,000 entering or leaving Canada; and (iii) source-jurisdiction exit controls (e.g., SAFE, RBI, or other central bank approval regimes) that the foreign parent must satisfy before remitting equity. The CAD is the functional currency of the BC entity; the USD is the most liquid counter-currency, with same-day spot execution and no central-bank conversion declaration requirement.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada imposes no statutory timeline, mandatory conversion ratio, or surrender obligation on export proceeds. A British Columbia ghost-kitchen operator may hold delivery-aggregator settlement receipts and trade proceeds in CAD, USD, or any foreign currency without restriction, and may convert or deploy them at commercial discretion. However, every Canadian financial intermediary must report to FINTRAC any electronic funds transfer of C$10,000 or more entering or leaving Canada within 24 hours, and the treasury operator must maintain a documented reconciliation of marketplace settlements (UberEats and DoorDash payouts) to the operating account. For physical goods crossing the border, CBSA export declarations apply under the Customs Act; for services or digital platform revenue, no export declaration is required.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operating Account (CAD/USD) with optional segregated Capital Contribution clearing account and delivery-aggregator settlement sub-ledger
Operating Account (CAD/USD) with commercial card and payables automation
Operating Account (CAD/USD) with dedicated trade-finance desk for Commercial Letters of Credit
Operating Account and FX forward facility under ISDA 2002 Master Agreement
Operating Account (CAD/USD) with SWIFT GPI outbound wire capability
Operating Account (CAD) with treasury and capital-markets desk

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: Medium (ancillary use only). Canada does not issue an EU-style electronic money institution (EMI) licence; a non-Canadian digital EMI must either partner with a Canadian Schedule I Bank or register as a Money Services Business (MSB) with FINTRAC and, where operating in British Columbia, comply with the federal PCMLTFA and the British Columbia Money Services Business Act (administered by Consumer Protection BC). Platforms such as Wise, Revolut Business, and Airwallex hold Canadian MSB registrations and can serve as secondary rails for low-value foreign vendor payments and FX conversion, but they are not chartered deposit-takers and cannot provide credit, escrow, settlement finality, or access to LVTS. The recommended treasury architecture is a primary Schedule I bank account paired with one registered MSB account used exclusively for low-value cross-border disbursements; funds must not remain as unregulated float, and the MSB should route CAD payouts through a Canadian clearing member to preserve auditability.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote opening is permitted in principle for Canadian-resident directors through PIPEDA-compliant video identity verification and notarized corporate documents. In practice, Schedule I banks require at least one in-branch or video appointment with a corporate banker, a wet-ink or e-signed board resolution and mandate, and certified copies of incorporation and registry documents. Non-resident directors are generally required to appear physically in a Canadian branch or to provide a sworn notarized identity exemplification with apostille, an economic-nexus declaration, and a professional banking reference from their home jurisdiction. Banks retain discretion to refuse fully remote opening for a delivery-only treasury entity. A physical appearance by the director or corporate secretary at a Vancouver branch, accompanied by the Certificate of Good Standing, Register of Directors, CRS/FATCA self-certifications, and a CPA-prepared opening package, materially shortens the 5-15 business day review period and is the strongest onboarding posture.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-ownership opacity: multiple 'virtual brands' operating under DBAs and franchisor marks, with no clear share-ownership chain between the Canadian operating entity and the ultimate foreign parent.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver (i) the BC Corporate Registry 'Filing History and Company Summary' extract naming all directors and registered office; (ii) a notarized Register of Directors and Register of Shareholders; (iii) a completed Beneficial Ownership Declaration identifying every natural-person ultimate owner; (iv) the franchise or licensing agreements with each virtual-brand owner; (v) a CPA-prepared organizational chart mapping each ghost brand to a legal entity and bank account; and (vi) certificates of good standing from upstream jurisdictions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity aggregated settlement from UberEats and DoorDash flowing into one account while outbound wires sweep funds to foreign suppliers or a parent in a low-tax jurisdiction, creating a 'shadow clearing' profile.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide (i) signed marketplace operator agreements with UberEats Canada and DoorDash Canada, including payout schedules and holdback terms; (ii) a treasury policy mandating single-entity settlement at the operating account; (iii) monthly reconciliation by an external CPA of marketplace settlement statements to bank records; (iv) underlying supplier invoices, purchase orders, and payment evidence for each outbound wire with HS codes and goods descriptions; (v) Canada Revenue Agency Form T106 (Information Return for Non-Arm's-Length Transactions) and intercompany service agreements evidencing arm's-length pricing; and (vi) an annual projected cash-flow budget demonstrating legitimate operating velocity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident directors and shareholders domiciled in jurisdictions on Financial Action Task Force (FATF) 'black' or 'grey' lists, or without economic nexus in Canada.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Assemble an Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) file: notarized passports and proof of residential address (utility statement plus bank reference in the home jurisdiction), independent source-of-wealth declaration supported by tax returns or audited financial statements of the shareholder, professional reference letters from home-jurisdiction banks, a Canadian police certificate for Canadian-resident directors, and a written economic-nexus memorandum demonstrating that the BC entity performs real functions (chef employment, kitchen leases, delivery integration) in British Columbia. The file must be escalated to the bank's Financial Crime Risk Unit (FCRU) rather than branch staff.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Split-injection of initial capital (multiple wires below C$10,000 from the foreign parent) or a mismatch between registry issued capital and actual paid-up capital observed in early account funding.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit (i) the unanimous shareholders' agreement and board resolution approving a single capital subscription and deposit schedule; (ii) the share subscription ledger filed with the BC Registry; (iii) SWIFT GPI payment confirmations including the Unique End-to-End Transaction Reference (UETR) and remitter bank reference; (iv) proof of source of funds from the parent's audited financial statements; (v) the remitting bank's compliance sign-off where available; and (vi) a written confirmation that funds will not be structured, with the company's banking authorization naming only one treasury signatory for inbound capital.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Settlement of 'ghost kitchen' commissions to a foreign franchisor or technology platform whose ownership overlaps with the ultimate parent (related-party service payments).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Present the master franchise and software subscription agreements with an independent valuation, a split of consideration for intellectual property versus data-processing services, a Canadian withholding-tax analysis (Form NR301 or treaty relief certification for reduced Part XIII withholding), and a transfer-pricing benchmark (CRA Form T106) supported by a comparability study prepared by a local accountant. Banks routinely clear related-party wires once the underlying service, tax disclosure, and arm's-length pricing evidence are in the file.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: the foreign investor initiates a single SWIFT MT103 (or MT202 interbank credit) from its home bank to the BC operating account, denominated in CAD or USD, with the field-72 narrative 'equity subscription / share capital issuance - Ghost Kitchen Operating Co.' and with no cash-splitting across dates or banks. Canada maintains no mandatory purpose-code or prior-approval regime for inbound capital, but the receiving Schedule I bank will treat the transfer as a FINTRAC reportable EFT (threshold C$10,000) and will require: (i) a statement of purpose; (ii) the share subscription agreement; (iii) a board resolution authorizing the issuance of shares; (iv) CRS/FATCA self-certification of the investor (Form NR301); and (v) if the investor is in an exit-capital-control jurisdiction, the home-state approval reference (e.g., SAFE ODI registration, RBI CAP/LRS approval, or other central bank remittance clearance) stated in field 72. Funds must not be split into smaller tranches to avoid the C$10,000 reporting threshold. Credits arrive subject to the bank's financial-crime screening; after clearance, the funds are recorded in the corporate share register and in the Canada Revenue Agency paid-up-capital tracking to avoid deemed benefit or thin-capitalization issues. For an intercompany loan, an interest-bearing note must be executed and Form T106 filed where the lender is non-arm's-length.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements use four primary clearing rails. (1) SWIFT MT103 with GPI UETR for supplier invoices and intercompany payments; each wire must carry the supplier's bank details, invoice number, and goods description with HS code to satisfy the bank's electronic funds transfer record-keeping and FINTRAC reporting rules. (2) Irrevocable Commercial Letters of Credit (UCP600) issued by the Vancouver trade-finance desk for high-value imported kitchen equipment and fit-out contracts; a confirmed LC is recommended for USD or CNY settlement with overseas suppliers. (3) Domestic CAD business-to-business payments via the Canadian Large Value Transfer System (LVTS) for same-day finality on rent, payroll tax remittances, and supplier payments above C$50,000; smaller recurring disbursements may use ACSS EFT or Interac RTP. (4) Delivery-aggregator settlements (UberEats and DoorDash payouts) arrive as aggregated EFT or ACH-style credits to the designated operating account per marketplace payout terms, often daily or weekly with a 7-30 day holdback; the treasury operation must maintain a sub-ledger allocating each settlement lump into the correct virtual brand management account, with marketplace fees, driver tips, and refunds tracked separately. Cross-currency conversion is centralized in the FX facility (forwards or spot) rather than executed inside the merchant account to reduce spreads. Cash, anonymous cards, and crypto rails are prohibited in this treasury architecture.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable OTC FX forward contracts (CAD/USD, CAD/EUR, CAD/CNH) under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with Schedule and Canadian Credit Support Annex, executed with a Schedule I Bank dealing desk; suitable for hedging confirmed foreign-currency supplier payables and marketplace receivables.

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) for hedging exposures in restricted-convertibility currencies (e.g., CNY, INR, TRY, BRL) where physical delivery is impractical; permitted as a Canadian corporate end-user under the business-purpose exemption and subject to the bank's FX middle-office credit approval.

Cross-currency swaps (FX swaps and cross-currency interest rate swaps) for matching a CAD-denominated operating line to USD-denominated revenue received from US-based meal-delivery aggregators, executed with a qualified counterparty and compliant with OSFI and Uncleared Margin Rules (UMR) threshold requirements where applicable.
Plain-vanilla European FX options and zero-premium collars (CAD/USD) purchased from a licensed bank to protect minimum settlement rates on high-volume delivery payouts.

CAD/USD futures and options on futures traded on a regulated exchange (CME) through a registered futures commission merchant, with hedge-designation documentation and variation margin funding recorded in the treasury ledger.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: BC Registrar of Companies, Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 2 months after each anniversary of incorporation under the BC Business Corporations Act, s. 372
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing for two consecutive anniversary dates permits the Registrar to strike the company; a struck company may be administratively dissolved after further notice; restoration requires payment of arrears and a restoration fee.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (federal and BC corporate tax return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) under the federal-provincial tax administration agreement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing due within 6 months after fiscal year-end; balance-due within 2 months after year-end for most corporations (3 months for an eligible Canadian-controlled private corporation claiming the small business deduction with taxable income under CA$500,000)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per complete month up to 12 months; repeated-failure penalty of 10% plus 2% per month; daily compound arrears interest at CRA prescribed rates.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual GST/HST Return (if the corporation is a GST/HST registrant)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual filers: within 3 months after the fiscal year-end; quarterly filers: within 1 month after each reporting period end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure-to-file penalty of 1% of unremitted net tax plus 25% of any additional balance; daily compound interest on amounts owing; possible mandatory electronic filing and registration consequences.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Municipal Business Licence Renewal (delivery-only food service operation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: City of Vancouver Business Licencing or applicable British Columbia municipality
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by March 31 for Vancouver; municipality-specific renewal window elsewhere in BC
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-renewal penalty of 50% of the annual licence fee; operating without a valid licence is a bylaw offence subject to fines, business closure, and licence revocation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Food Service Establishment Permit Renewal (health operating permit)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Regional health authority under the BC Food Premises Regulation (e.g., Vancouver Coastal Health, Fraser Health)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the permit anniversary or health-authority inspection schedule; a valid permit is required for lawful operation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Permit suspension or revocation; administrative orders to correct hazards; prohibition of food operations; daily penalties under the Public Health Act and Food Premises Regulation for continuing contraventions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements filing to BC Corporate Registry (new statutory mandate)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Effective May 1, 2027; filing due within 6 months after the company's fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing administrative penalties prescribed by regulation; persistent non-filing may be treated as a registry delinquency and lead to strike-off proceedings.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No revenue-based compulsory audit threshold under the BC Business Corporations Act. An auditor must be appointed at each annual general meeting unless all voting shareholders consent by resolution to waive appointment for that fiscal year; private ghost kitchen corporations commonly waive the audit. Lenders or platform agreements may contractually require a financial statement review or audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as issued by the Canadian Accounting Standards Board (AcSB) applies to publicly accountable enterprises; a private BC corporation may elect ASPE (CPA Canada Handbook Part II) for unlisted financial statements, with revenue recognition under ASPE Section 3400.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: BC has no separate annual UBO filing. The Individual Transparency Register must be updated within 15 days of any transfer or change in significant control (25% or more of shares/votes or de facto control); before each BC Annual Report, directors must verify that the register is accurate, and the annual report attests to the company records. Administrative penalties up to CA$25,000 may apply to individuals; corporate penalties apply for register defaults.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$150 - US$350 per year for the services of a BC-licensed registered office and corporate records agent
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$2,500 - US$6,000 per year for a private-enterprise compilation/review engagement in BC; full audit between US$8,000 and US$25,000 for a small virtual-brand ghost kitchen
